Dear Project Blackbird team,

I’m writing on behalf of the Sabrina Audrey Milone Foundation (Smile Like Sab), established in memory of Sabrina Audrey Milone. Our focus includes mental health awareness, eating disorder research and support, and community-building initiatives.

Project Blackbird’s aim to de-stigmatize eating-disorder and mental-health conversation within underrepresented communities resonates with those purposes. We learned about your gala at the International Spy Museum in Washington, D.C., and would appreciate learning more about your programs and their impact.

Our current sponsor search is focused on Manhattan, so your gala falls outside that scope. Should our board consider broader collaboration, we would want to understand the available pathways first. We also encountered references to gala sponsorship and program-book advertising, but have not confirmed whether those options are available.

Would you be willing to share a brief program overview and clarify whether there are opportunities for another foundation to explore collaboration? We are seeking information only and are not committing to funding or participation.

Thank you for your consideration.

WithAll’s eating-disorder recovery and prevention work aligns with those purposes. We learned about your Keys in Bloom Gala in Golden Valley, Minnesota, and would welcome a better understanding of the programs it supports and their impact.

Our current sponsor research is focused on Manhattan, so the gala is outside that geographic scope. If our board considers broader opportunities, information about your stated event sponsorship options and any cross-organization collaboration pathways would help us assess relevance. Would you be willing to share a brief overview of your programs and available ways for another foundation to learn more or explore collaboration?
